extracted.intended_audience: Medicare providers, hospital administrators, transplant hospitals (THs), organ procurement organizations (OPOs/IOPOs), histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs), Medicare contractors, GME program directors, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of substantive regulatory requirements and definitional standards from CMS/CFR amendments governing provider cost finding, GME program approval and nondiscrimination, organ acquisition reimbursement (IOPO/HCL), payment reconciliation, device pass-through eligibility, CEHRT definitions, and episode-based target price calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider request to change cost finding method
rubrics_metrics.description: A provider that wishes to change its cost finding method must submit a request to its contractor, in writing, 90 days prior to the end of the cost reporting period to which the provider's request for change applies. The contractor's determination will be furnished in writing and is binding on the provider as of the date of the contractor's written notice. When the contractor approves the provider's request to change methods, the provider must use this method for the cost reporting period to which the request applies and for all subsequent cost reporting periods, unless the contractor approves a subsequent request by the provider to change its cost finding methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation when creating multiple administrative/general cost centers
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating multiple administrative and general cost centers, a provider must track and allocate overhead expenses based on actual resource consumption and use accurate statistics to allocate its costs to ensure overhead costs are accurately assigned to departments benefiting from the services provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved geriatric program definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved geriatric program means, subject to the requirements in §413.84, a fellowship program of one or more years in length that is approved by one of the national organizations listed in §415.152 under that respective organization's criteria for geriatric fellowship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved medical residency program definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved medical residency program means, subject to the requirements in §413.84, a program that meets one of the following criteria: (i) is approved by one of the national organizations listed in §415.152; (ii) may count towards certification of the participant in a specialty or subspecialty listed in the Directory of Graduate Medical Education Programs (AMA) or the Annual Report and Reference Handbook (ABMS); or (iii) is approved by the ACGME or other organization designated by the Secretary as a fellowship program in geriatric medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and cap rules for new medical residency training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §413.79, a new medical residency training program receives initial accreditation or begins training on or after January 1, 1995 and, effective for programs started on or after October 1, 2026, at least 90 percent of individual residents that participate in the program during the 5-year cap building period must not have previous experience training in another program in the same specialty, subject to exclusions and exceptions. The 90% requirement excludes individuals who (i) with previous experience enter as first-year residents through the National Resident Matching Program or another binding third-party matching program, or (ii) meet the definition of a “displaced resident.” The 90% requirement does not apply to programs accredited for 16 or fewer resident positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to cap-building period for new urban and rural programs as defined in §413.79(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against unlawful discrimination by approved programs
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved medical residency training program or an approved nursing and allied health education program must not discriminate, or promote or encourage discrimination, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including the use of those characteristics or intentional proxies for those characteristics as a selection criterion for employment, program participation, resource allocation, or similar activities, opportunities, or benefits (see §413.84(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against discriminatory criteria by accrediting organizations and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: An accrediting organization of approved medical residency training programs or of approved nursing and allied health education programs, and any publications cited in the regulations that list specialties or subspecialties of such programs, must not use criteria that discriminate, or promote or encourage discrimination, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including the use of those characteristics or intentional proxies as selection criteria (see §413.84(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of programs excluded only for discriminatory or abortion-related accreditation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved medical residency training programs and approved nursing and allied health education programs include programs that would be accredited except for the accrediting agency's reliance upon an accreditation standard that requires an entity to (1) discriminate or promote/encourage discrimination on protected bases, or (2) perform, require, provide, or refer for training in the performance of induced abortions, or make arrangements for such training, regardless of exceptions or exemptions (see §413.84(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net cost determination for approved educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to §413.84, the net cost of approved educational activities is determined by: (A) determining allowable direct costs incurred by the provider for trainee stipends and compensation of faculty employed by the provider; (B) subtracting revenues the provider receives from students or on behalf of students (e.g., tuition, student fees, textbooks purchased for resale); and (C) allocating indirect costs of the activities as determined under Medicare cost-finding principles in §413.24, limited to costs the provider itself incurs as a consequence of operating the approved educational activities (see §413.85(d)(2)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from allowable direct and indirect educational costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct and indirect allowable costs of educational activities do not include patient care costs, costs incurred by a related organization, costs that constitute a redistribution of costs from an educational institution to a provider, or costs that have been or are currently being provided through community support (see §413.85(d)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for considering an activity an approved nursing and allied health education program
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to §413.84, CMS will consider an activity an approved nursing and allied health education program if the program is a planned program of study that is licensed by State law, or if licensing is not required, is accredited by the recognized national professional organization for the particular activity (see §413.85(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable organ acquisition costs (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs recognized as allowable in organ acquisition include costs incurred in the acquisition of organs intended for transplant, including organs subsequently determined unsuitable for transplant and furnished for research, from living or deceased donors by the hospital or from deceased donors by an OPO. Administrative and general costs that may be allowable and included on the cost report for an OPO or a transplant hospital (TH) can also be recognized. Costs incurred by OPOs for public education within their donation service area and professional education are allowable overhead costs included on the OPO cost report (see §413.402(a) and (b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of OPO-sponsored seminar costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs associated with and incurred for OPO-sponsored seminars where continuing education credits are given and where the attendee is not on the OPO's staff are allowable overhead costs (see §413.402(d)(2)(v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registry fees included in average organ acquisition cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Registry fees as specified in §413.402(b)(6) are included in the average organ acquisition cost (see §413.404(b)(3)(ii)(C)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO organ-specific Standard Acquisition Charge (SAC) — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For each organ type, the contractor establishes the organ-specific SAC based on an estimate of initial year projected or subsequent years' actual, reasonable and necessary costs that the IOPO expects to incur to procure deceased donor organs during the IOPO's cost reporting period, divided by the initial year projected or subsequent years' actual number of usable deceased donor organs the IOPO expects to procure (see §413.404(d)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO initial-year SAC development
rubrics_metrics.description: For each organ type, the contractor develops the IOPO's initial organ-specific SAC based on the IOPO's budget information (see §413.404(d)(1)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO subsequent-year SAC computation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each organ type, the contractor computes the organ-specific SAC for subsequent years using the IOPO's costs related to organ acquisition that were incurred in the prior cost reporting period and dividing those costs by the number of usable deceased donor organs procured during that cost reporting period (see §413.404(d)(1)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ SACs as interim payments and contractor adjustment authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Each organ-specific SAC amount is the organ-specific interim payment the TH or other OPO pays to the IOPO. Only the contractor may adjust the organ SACs. IOPOs may request that the contractor make an adjustment in accordance with §413.64(e), or the contractor may initiate an adjustment in accordance with §413.64(d)(2) or §413.64(e) (see §413.404(d)(1)(iii) and (v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs that may be used to develop IOPO deceased donor SACs (non-exhaustive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs that may be used include, but are not limited to: costs of organs acquired from other THs or OPOs; transportation costs as specified in §413.402(b)(8); surgeons' fees for excising deceased donor organs (limited to $1,250 for kidneys); tissue typing services (including independent laboratories); organ preservation and perfusion costs; general routine and special care service costs (e.g., ICU/CCU related to the donor); operating room and inpatient ancillary service costs (see §413.404(d)(1)(iv)(A)-(G)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing SACs when IOPO obtains organ from another IOPO
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IOPO obtains an organ from another IOPO, the receiving IOPO is responsible for paying the procuring IOPO's SAC. The receiving IOPO uses its SAC for each organ type, and not the procuring IOPO's SAC, when billing the TH receiving the organ (see §413.404(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement principles for IOPOs and HCLs (kidney and non-renal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered services furnished by IOPOs and HCLs in connection with organ acquisition and transplantation are reimbursed under the principles for determining reasonable cost: (i) For kidney acquisition and transplantation services, IOPOs and HCLs are reimbursed under the principles for determining reasonable cost; (ii) For non-renal organ acquisition and transplantation services furnished for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027, IOPOs and HCLs are reimbursed under the principles for determining reasonable cost (see §413.420(a)(1)). Services furnished by IOPOs and HCLs that have an agreement with the Secretary are paid directly by the TH or OPO using a kidney SAC (for an IOPO) or contractor-established rates (for an HCL) (see §413.420(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements required for IOPO/HCL Medicare reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IOPO or HCL that wishes to have the cost of its pre-transplant services reimbursed under Medicare must file an agreement with CMS under which the IOPO or HCL agrees, among other things, to: permit CMS to designate a contractor to determine the interim reimbursement rate and Medicare's reasonable cost based upon the cost report filed by the IOPO/HCL; and to pay to CMS amounts received or receivable that are determined to be in excess of the reasonable cost of services provided (see §413.420(c)(1) and (c)(1)(ii) and (iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim rate establishment and use for IOPOs/HCLs
rubrics_metrics.description: THs with approved transplant programs and OPOs pay IOPOs or HCLs for pre-transplantation services on the basis of interim rates established by the contractor. Interim rates are contractor-established rates based on costs associated with procuring organs incurred by an IOPO or HCL during its previous fiscal year. If there is not adequate cost data to determine the initial interim rate, the contractor determines it according to the IOPO's or HCL's estimate of projected costs for the fiscal year. For non-renal organs, interim rates for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027 will be contractor-established non-renal organ-specific SACs or contractor-established rates (see §413.420(d)(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation of interim payments and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments or amounts payable based on interim rates are reconciled directly with the IOPO or HCL after the close of the IOPO's or HCL's fiscal year in accordance with §413.420(e). Retroactive adjustments are made in accordance with §413.64(f). Lump sum adjustments are made directly between the contractor and IOPO/HCL if determination of reasonable cost reveals overpayment or underpayment (see §413.420(e)(2)(i)-(ii) and (3)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and new interim rate establishment for cost periods beginning Oct 1, 2027
rubrics_metrics.description: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027, a cost report submitted by an IOPO or HCL is reviewed by the contractor and new interim reimbursement rates for non-renal organ acquisition costs for the subsequent fiscal year are established by the contractor based upon this review (see §413.420(e)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals for IOPO/HCL cost determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amount in controversy is $1,000 or more, any IOPO or HCL that disagrees with a contractor's cost determination under §413.420 is entitled to a contractor hearing, review of the contractor hearing officer's decision by a CMS reviewing official, and Administrator Review in accordance with applicable procedures (§§405.1801(b)(2) and 405.1811 through 405.1834) (see §413.420(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved graduate medical education (GME) program definition for §415.152
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved GME program means, subject to the requirements in §413.84, a residency program approved by the ACGME, the American Osteopathic Association, the Commission on Dental Accreditation of the ADA, the Council on Podiatric Medical Education of the American Podiatric Medical Association, or other organization determined by the Secretary (see §415.152).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pass-through pathway for certain medical devices
rubrics_metrics.description: For devices for which pass-through payment status began on or after January 1, 2020 and on or before January 1, 2028 for applications received through September 30, 2026, as an alternative pathway the device is part of the FDA's Breakthrough Devices Program and has received marketing authorization for the indication covered by the Breakthrough Device designation (see §419.66(c)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified electronic health record technology (CEHRT) criteria (2019–2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 2019 through 2026, CEHRT includes 45 CFR 170.315(a)(12) (family health history) and 45 CFR 170.315(e)(3) (patient health information capture). For 2019 through 2026, the applicable measure calculation certification criterion at 45 CFR 170.315(g)(1) or (2) applies for all certification criteria that support a meaningful use objective with a percentage-based measure (see §495.4(2)(i) and (ii)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: APC update factor, MS-DRG update factor, updated prospective trend factor
rubrics_metrics.description: APC update factor: component applied to the prospective trend factor to ensure APC weights corresponding to the performance year are incorporated into target price calculations (§512.505). MS-DRG update factor: component applied to the prospective trend factor for episodes with anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end dates in the fourth quarter of the performance year to account for changes in MS-DRG definitions and weights (§512.505). Updated prospective trend factor: multiplier incorporated into the preliminary target price to estimate changes in spending patterns between the baseline period and the corresponding calendar year and fiscal year in the performance year, calculated as set forth in §512.540(b)(7) (§512.505).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spinal fusion episode and procedure definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Spinal fusion means any cervical, thoracic, or lumbar spinal fusion procedure paid through specified IPPS MS-DRGs (listed) and, on or after October 1, 2026, additional MS-DRGs (523–525), or the OPPS under HCPCS codes 22551, 22554, 22612, 22630, or 22633 (§512.505).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode determination for CJR-X with TEAM participant
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary is in a CJR-X episode if the beneficiary has a procedure performed at a TEAM participant during the 90-day post-discharge period after a CJR-X anchor hospitalization or CJR-X anchor procedure (see §512.537(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective normalization factor computation
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates a prospective normalization factor at the MS-DRG/HCPCS region level to ensure that the average of the total risk-adjusted benchmark price does not exceed the average of the total non-risk adjusted benchmark price by: (i) applying risk adjustment multipliers to baseline episodes to calculate estimated risk-adjusted target price; and (ii) dividing the mean of the benchmark price for each episode across all hospitals and regions by the mean of the estimated risk-adjusted benchmark price for the same episode types across all hospitals and regions (§512.540(b)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective trend factor calculation (regional & national)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prospective trend factor for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region is the average of the multiplier for that region and the national average. CMS calculates a multiplier using linear regression on the logarithmically transformed average regional spending for each episode type across baseline and trend years at regional and national level, exponentiates the coefficient to get estimated annual change, and squares that value to get the 2-year prospective trend factor (§512.540(b)(7)(i)(A)-(D)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated prospective trend factor composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated prospective trend factor is calculated as the product of: (A) the prospective trend factor; (B) the APC update factor (ratio of benchmark prices with APC weights corresponding to the calendar year of the performance year to benchmark prices with APC weights of the prior year); and (C) the MS-DRG update factor (for episodes with anchor dates in the fourth quarter, ratio of benchmark prices with second fiscal year inputs to benchmark prices with first fiscal year inputs) (§512.540(b)(7)(ii)(A)-(C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of preliminary target prices and update factors
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS communicates the preliminary target prices for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type for each region and for each TEAM participant before the performance year in which they apply. CMS communicates the APC and MS-DRG update factors after the corresponding calendar year and second fiscal year inputs are published with the applicable final payment rules (§512.540(b)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment and application of first/second fiscal year MS-DRG inputs at reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: At reconciliation, preliminary target prices computed under §512.540 are risk adjusted by applying beneficiary-level and hospital-level risk adjustment factors specific to the beneficiary in the episode. CMS applies coefficients estimated with the assigned first fiscal year MS-DRG/HCPCS inputs for episodes with anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end dates in the fourth quarter of a performance year. Episodes in the fourth quarter are calculated specific to assigned first and second fiscal year MS-DRG/HCPCS combinations (see §512.545(d)(1), (e)(1)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on applied normalization factor (±5 percent)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applied, the adjustment described cannot exceed ±5 percent of the prospective normalization factor (as specified in §512.540(b)(6)) (§512.545(e)(1)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capped retrospective trend factor and ±3 percent cap
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates a capped retrospective trend factor for each episode type and region to apply during reconciliation. The retrospective trend factor is the average regional capped performance year episode spending divided by the average regional capped baseline period episode spending. The retrospective trend factor is capped so that the maximum difference cannot exceed ±3 percent of the updated prospective trend factor (§512.545(f)(1)-(2)). The capped retrospective trend factor is then applied to normalized, risk-adjusted target prices to calculate reconciliation target prices (§512.545(f)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measures and composite quality score baseline periods for performance years 4 and 5
rubrics_metrics.description: For performance year 4 and 5 CMS specifies a set of quality measures for all episode categories (including Hybrid Hospital-Wide All-Cause Readmission Measure CMIT #356; Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury CMIT #1518; Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure CMIT #1788; Thirty-day Risk-Standardized Death Rate among Surgical Inpatients with Complications ISCMR CMIT #134) and for LEJR episodes (THA/TKA PRO-PM CMIT #1618) and LEJR/Spinal Fusion (Information Transfer PRO-PM CMIT #1797) with specified CQS baseline periods for each measure (§512.547(a)(4)-(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists explicit baseline periods for each measure and performance year; CMS will use these for composite quality score calculation and display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of first fiscal year MS-DRG for fourth-quarter anchor episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS assigns a first fiscal year MS-DRG by identifying diagnosis or procedure codes that change between the first and second fiscal year of the performance year per the fiscal year final payment rule MS-DRG definitions, for each episode with an anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end date in the fourth quarter of a performance year (§512.550(c)(1)).
